sources.entry: Noto - Plain text editor for macOS with customizable themes.

summary.one_liner: Noto is a plain text editor for macOS written in Swift, with customizable color themes.
summary.what_it_does: Noto is a plain text editor for macOS, written in Swift. It supports customizable color themes and an adjustable tab width. It includes a characters, words, and lines counter and supports various encodings. It offers advanced indentation with multiple-selection support. Printing is configurable: you can print with or without theme colors, rewrap contents to fit the page at 100% zoom, and show line numbers. The README lists touch bar support and multi-caret editing as planned but not yet implemented.
use_cases: editing plain text files on a Mac
writing notes or code in a simple editor
counting words, characters, or lines in a document
printing text with or without theme colors
opening files in various text encodings
how_to_run: Download a compiled binary from Noto's homepage (URL not given in README)
git clone the project (repository URL is truncated in README)
Compile and launch in Xcode using ⌘R
notable: Configurable printing options including theme colors and line numbers
Built-in characters, words, and lines counter
caveats: Requires macOS and Xcode 9 to compile from source
Touch bar support and multi-caret editing are planned but not implemented
README states the project is under slow development
